la:adj:gnarus.gloss: having knowledge of a thing; acquainted with a thing., skillful, practiced
senses: having knowledge of a thing; acquainted with a thing., skillful, practiced
la:adj:gnarus.html:
gnārus, a, um (also ante- and postclass. form gnārŭris, e, ; ; ; ; and cf.: gnaruris γνώριμος, Gloss. Philox.—Another form is † nārus, like navus, notus, acc. to ), adj.
Sanscr. gna-, ganāmi, know; Gr. γιγνώσκω; Lat. gnosco, nosco, narrare, etc.
,
knowing or acquainted with a thing; skilful, practised, expert (syn. doctus, eruditus, peritus).
Lit. (rare but class.); constr. with gen., or with a rel. or object-clause; ante- and post-class. with acc.
With gen.: nec loci gnara sum,: loci, ap. P.; rei publicae,: armorum et militiae, § 4: artis,: temporis,; cf. : si modo vinitor gnarus est iis utendi,: nostri tergi,: venandi,.—
With rel.clause: Periclem uberem et fecundum fuisse, gnarumque, quibus orationis modis, etc.,: nemine gnaro aut opinante, quidnam coepturus esset,.—
With object-clause: Hasdrubal satis gnarus, Hannibalem transitus quosdam pretio mercatum,; cf. ; ; ; : concha cum manum videt, comprimit sese operitque opes suas, gnara propter illas se peti,.—
With acc.: simul gnarures vos volo esse hanc rem mecum,: ut mecum sitis gnarures,.—
Transf., pass., known (for the usual notus; post-Aug.; very rare, except in Tac.): in paludem gnaram vincentibus,: idque nulli magis gnarum quam Neroni,; cf.: gnarum id Caesari, (opp. incognita), .—Absol.: conspicui eoque gnari,.—Comp. not in use.—Sup.,

la:noun:gnomon.html:
gnōmon, ŏnis, m., = γνώμων,
the pin or style of a sundial, the gnomon, ; ; ; .
